lab02-s000.title: Before You Begin
lab02-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 25 minutes
**What you will create:** A $30 million top-down target allocated using the previous year's revenue mix, a bottom-up sales plan incorporating regional adjustments, and a workflow that separates the submission status from two approval stages: regional and headquarters. ---

lab02-s001.title: Where This Module Fits
lab02-s001.markdown:
Management's FY26 revenue target is **$30 million**. Harborlight's actual FY25 revenue was approximately **$25.9 million**. Where will the roughly $4 million difference come from? Your role in this module is to make that answer concrete.

You will first establish the overall framework through top-down allocation, then let managers with local knowledge make bottom-up adjustments. Along the way, you will try **locking**, an important feature in real planning work.

The target deliberately increases in two stages. Management's initial target was $28.5 million, an increase of roughly 10%, but it was subsequently raised to $30 million, an increase of roughly 16%. First allocate the initial target, then lock the quarters that are already finalized. Allocate the additional amount only to periods where adjustments are still possible.

Use the `Plan Intro` sheet you created in Module 01.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Series names and planning-year date keys are separate.** In this exercise, `2026 Target` and `2026 Sales Plan` are names of series copied from FY25 actuals. Naming a series does not move the year and month keys in the Date hierarchy to 2026. Here, you will **practice target allocation and adjustment using the 2025 timeline**. A plan saved against actual FY26 dates, or a plan-versus-actual comparison aligned by fiscal year, requires a separate design for the date keys and the periods covered by the planning data.

---

lab02-s002.title: Create an Editable Column
lab02-s002.markdown:
1. On the **Planning** ribbon, select **Totals**. Open the **Column Grand Total** dropdown and change the default **Off** to **Left**. A **Grand Total** column summing actuals across all FY25 periods appears to the left of the period columns.

   ![Totals menu with Column Grand Total set to Off](../assets/screenshots/lab02/01-totals-menu.png)

   ![Selecting Left from the Column Grand Total options](../assets/screenshots/lab02/02-grandtotal-left-option.png)

   ![Grand Total column added on the left, showing 25.87M on the All row, the same as the 2025 column](../assets/screenshots/lab02/03-grandtotal-enabled.png)

> [!TIP]
> **Review these terms, which appear frequently below.** The **grand total column** is this annual total column. A **grand total cell** is the intersection of that column and a particular row. On the *All* row, it represents the company-wide annual total; on the *Energy & Sports* row, it represents that subcategory's annual total. Entering a value here also allocates it to the underlying detail.
>
> The grand total column and the *2025* column display the same numbers. Because *2025 Gross Revenue* is a single-year measure, the total across all periods equals the total for that year. The distinction becomes clearer when you expand to quarters in the next section.

2. On the **Planning** ribbon, select **Number** → **Copy from another series** → **2025 Gross Revenue**.

   ![Opening Copy from another series under Number and selecting 2025 Gross Revenue](../assets/screenshots/lab02/04-copy-series-menu.png)

3. Click the **Title** field in the **Data Input** pane and use **Ctrl+A → Backspace** to remove the default `Number`. Confirm the field is empty, then enter `2026 Target`.

   ![Data Input defaults: Title Number, Visual Measure, Number, Sum for both aggregations, and parent-to-child distribution checked](../assets/screenshots/lab02/05-data-input-defaults.png)

4. Confirm that **Title** contains only `2026 Target`. Leave **Insert as: Visual Measure**, **Input type: Number**, **Column aggregation type: Sum**, **Row aggregation type: Sum**, and **Distribute parent value to children: checked**, then select **Create**.

   ![Title changed to 2026 Target with default input, aggregation, and distribution settings retained](../assets/screenshots/lab02/06-target-settings.png)

   ![Measure created successfully message and FY25 baseline values copied into the 2026 Target columns](../assets/screenshots/lab02/07-target-created.png)

> [!NOTE]
> The default **Title** may be `Number`. Typing without removing the existing text produces an unintended name. Before creating the series, confirm that the entire field contains only `2026 Target`.

The new column **starts with a copy of the FY25 values**. The total is approximately $25.9 million. This is the starting point for the plan, not the target.

<details>
<summary>What the other settings mean and why this exercise uses their defaults</summary>

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Insert as** | Visual Measure | Inserts a column for each category when a column hierarchy exists. This sheet uses the Date hierarchy in Columns, so Visual Measure is appropriate for displaying the measure in each period. Visual Column inserts only one column, regardless of the hierarchy |
| **Input type** | Number | A suitable type for entering monetary amounts |
| **Column aggregation type** | Sum | Specifies how values in the column hierarchy are aggregated |
| **Row aggregation type** | Sum | Specifies how values in the row hierarchy are aggregated |
| **Distribute parent value to children** | On | **A prerequisite for this module.** Automatically allocates a parent's value to its child members proportionally. If off, entering $28.5 million in the grand total will not allocate it to regions or categories |
| **Enable Multi-Dimension Allocation** | No breakdown added | In the screen used here, **Add Breakdown** appeared under this heading. It supports allocation across multiple dimensions, but you will not add one in this exercise |
| **Minimum / Maximum Value** | None | Allows optional lower and upper limits for input values at the lowest level |

Before selecting **Create**, check these two points:

- **After creating a column, you cannot change Insert as or Input type.** The other settings can be edited later.
- **Distribute parent value to children** is available with Sum, Average (Leaf), Minimum, Maximum, First, and Last aggregation. Switching to another aggregation method disables allocation.

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> Native columns are read-only. You cannot enter values directly into a measure retrieved from the semantic model. Copying creates an editable series while retaining FY25 actuals as a comparison baseline. You will repeat this operation in later modules.

lab02-s003.title: Allocate the Target
lab02-s003.markdown:
Enter a number in one cell and let Planning build the plan throughout the underlying hierarchy.

**First, identify the cell to edit.** It is the intersection of these two items on screen:

- The **All** row: the top-level row aggregating all regions and categories.
- The **grand total column** for **2026 Target**: the annual total column displayed by enabling *Column Grand Total* in step 1. It is not a monthly column.

This cell currently shows company-wide FY25 actual revenue, approximately **25.9M**. It represents the overall total.

5. Double-click this cell and inspect the original value in the formula bar. In the sample data, the display is 25.87M, but the original value is **`25866900.4`**. Since you are replacing it with a new target, enter `28.5m` and press **Enter**. The input preview shows 28,500,000.

   ![Target All-row edit bar showing the unrounded value 25866900.4](../assets/screenshots/lab02/08-target-original-precision.png)

   ![Entering 28.5m with the input preview showing 28,500,000](../assets/screenshots/lab02/09-target-input-28-5m.png)

> [!NOTE]
> A single click only selects the cell. Double-click to edit it.
>
> The suffix `m` means million, or 1,000,000. When the display unit is already millions, as in this sheet, entering just `28.5` produces the same result. Including the suffix still makes your intent explicit, independent of the current display unit.

You have replaced the roughly $25.9 million baseline with management's initial target, an increase of approximately 10%. Planning allocates this value across all regions, categories, and subcategories **in proportion to the FY25 revenue mix**.

![Values saved message with Target at All 28.50M, Americas 7.87M, Asia Pacific 10.75M, and Energy & Sports 0.54M](../assets/screenshots/lab02/10-target-28-5m-result.png)

For more screen space, select the collapse arrows in the **Fields** and **Data** headings. Both panes are collapsed in the post-entry screenshot above.

**Sample calculation:** 28,500,000 / 25,866,900.40 is approximately 1.101794. Think of allocation as a ratio to the original value, not to the rounded display of 25.87M.

| Row | FY25 Actual | 2026 Target |
|---|---|---|
| All | 25.87 | **28.50** |
| Americas | 7.14 | **7.87** |
| Asia Pacific | 9.76 | **10.75** |
| Energy & Sports | 0.49 | **0.54** |

If the result is unexpected, such as only the All row changing, do not immediately delete the column. Check that the source is **2025 Gross Revenue**, that you are editing the correct series and grand total cell, that **Distribute parent value to children** is enabled, and that locks or filters are not restricting the scope. Check and correct the settings and scope, then compare the before-and-after values.

Entering a single number creates a plan allocated down to the detail. This is the basic top-down planning operation.

lab02-s004.title: Lock the First Half
lab02-s004.markdown:
Harborlight has already finalized its Q1 and Q2 plans. Promotions are arranged, and supply plans cannot change. Any additional growth must be allocated to the second half.

6. Hover over the **2025** column heading and select the **Expand/Collapse** arrow that appears to expand to quarters. In the sample data, the All-row Target values for Q1 through Q4 are **6.49 / 7.09 / 7.31 / 7.60M**.

   ![2025 expanded to quarters after the 28.5M allocation, with Target Q1 through Q4 at 6.49, 7.09, 7.31, and 7.60M](../assets/screenshots/lab02/11-quarterly-28-5m.png)

7. Select the **Q1** total cell for **2026 Target** (where the *All* row intersects Q1). Open the allocation icon menu on the right of the cell and select **Lock all children**, not **Lock this cell**. Repeat for **Q2**, and confirm that the Target descendants of both quarters turn gray. Do not confuse this with the background color of native actuals columns.

   ![Selecting Target Q1 on the All row and choosing Lock all children from the allocation menu](../assets/screenshots/lab02/12-lock-q1-menu.png)

   ![Choosing Lock all children for Target Q2 as well](../assets/screenshots/lab02/13-lock-q2-menu.png)

   ![Target descendants of Q1 and Q2 shown in gray](../assets/screenshots/lab02/14-q1-q2-locked.png)

8. Double-click the **2026 Target** annual grand total cell you edited earlier and enter `30m`. Confirm the input preview is 30,000,000, then press **Enter**. In the screen used here, **Values saved** appeared and the annual grand total became 30.00M.

   ![Entering 30m in the annual grand total after locking and confirming the 30,000,000 preview](../assets/screenshots/lab02/15-target-input-30m.png)

   ![After saving, Target is 30.00M annually, with Q1 through Q4 at 6.49, 7.09, 8.05, and 8.37M](../assets/screenshots/lab02/16-target-30m-locked-result.png)

Management's target has increased from $28.5 million to $30 million, and **the additional $1.5 million is allocated only to Q3 and Q4**. Q1 and Q2 remain unchanged.

**Check the result.** Compare the *All* row's quarterly totals before and after the change.

| Quarter | After allocating $28.5 million | After locking Q1 and Q2 and changing to $30 million |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | 6.49 | **6.49** (unchanged) |
| Q2 | 7.09 | **7.09** (unchanged) |
| Q3 | 7.31 | **8.05** |
| Q4 | 7.60 | **8.37** |

The increase is approximately 735,342.33 for Q3 and 764,657.67 for Q4, totaling $1.5 million. In millions to two decimal places, these are approximately 0.74 and 0.76. The allocation between Q3 and Q4 retains their proportions of the previous year's actuals.

> [!NOTE]
> **Caution when summing displayed values:** Calculating from the sample data's original precision gives Q3 approximately 7,311,492.347 after allocating 28.5M, displayed as 7.31 in millions to two decimal places. Summing the rounded quarterly displays may give 28.49; use unrounded values to assess the annual grand total.

Without locking, all four quarters would be recalculated at a ratio of 30,000,000 / 25,866,900.40. Q1 would become 6,835,517.181…, changing from 6.49 to **6.84** in millions to two decimal places. The original source's 6.83 has been corrected based on a calculation using the original precision. Simply entering a target at the top of the sheet would overwrite already-finalized promotional plans.

Locking protects finalized plans from such changes. A top-down revision without locks can unintentionally overwrite agreed plans.

9. Select the **Q1** total cell and choose **Unlock all children** in the allocation menu. This is different from **Unlock this cell**. Unlock **Q2** the same way, and confirm that removing the gray shading from Target does not change the annual grand total of 30.00M or the quarterly values.

   ![Choosing Unlock all children for Target Q1](../assets/screenshots/lab02/17-unlock-q1-menu.png)

   ![Choosing Unlock all children for Target Q2 as well](../assets/screenshots/lab02/18-unlock-q2-menu.png)

   ![After unlocking both quarters, annual 30.00M and quarterly 6.49, 7.09, 8.05, and 8.37M remain unchanged](../assets/screenshots/lab02/19-unlocked-target-result.png)

   To inspect the values more closely, double-click each quarter, read the edit bar, and close it with **Escape** without changing the value. In this example, the sample data's edit values are shown to five decimal places.

   | Quarter | Edit-bar display after unlocking | Expected value used for comparison |
   |---|---:|---|
   | Q1 | 6493741.32182 | Q1 from the 28.5M allocation, rounded to five decimal places |
   | Q2 | 7091792.21025 | Q2 from the 28.5M allocation, rounded to five decimal places |
   | Q3 | 8046834.67702 | Q3 from allocating 30M with Q1 and Q2 fixed, rounded to five decimal places |
   | Q4 | 8367631.79091 | Q4 from allocating 30M with Q1 and Q2 fixed, rounded to five decimal places |

<details>
<summary>Examples of values in the quarterly edit bars</summary>

![Q1 edit bar showing 6493741.32182](../assets/screenshots/lab02/20-q1-retained-precision.png)

![Q2 edit bar showing 7091792.21025](../assets/screenshots/lab02/21-q2-retained-precision.png)

![Q3 edit bar showing 8046834.67702](../assets/screenshots/lab02/22-q3-allocated-precision.png)

![Q4 edit bar showing 8367631.79091](../assets/screenshots/lab02/23-q4-allocated-precision.png)

</details>

**Save and reload.** Select **Save** at the top right, wait for the Saving indicator to disappear, then reload the browser. In the sample data example, `Plan Intro`, the Target series, All 30.00M, and quarterly 6.49 / 7.09 / 8.05 / 8.37M appear after reloading. If in Reading mode, switch to **Editing** at the top right to continue.

![After saving and reloading, Target 30.00M, quarterly values, and layout retained even in Reading mode](../assets/screenshots/lab02/24-target-reloaded.png)

> [!TIP]
> Unlock the cells when allocation is finished. If quarters remain locked, they will also be excluded from the next allocation. This can cause unexpected results later.

---

lab02-s005.title: Part 2: Build a Bottom-Up Plan
lab02-s005.markdown:
The target sets the overall framework. The plan, by contrast, contains the numbers each region commits to delivering.

1. On the **Planning** ribbon, select **Number** → **Copy from another series** → **2025 Gross Revenue**. Even if **2026 Target** is among the sources, **do not select it**. As in Part 1, select and delete all existing text in Title, then enter only `2026 Sales Plan`. Retain **Visual Measure / Number / Column aggregation type: Sum / Row aggregation type: Sum / Distribute parent value to children: checked**, and select **Create**.

   ![Actuals and Target listed as copy sources, with 2025 Gross Revenue selected](../assets/screenshots/lab02/25-sales-copy-source.png)

   ![Title set to 2026 Sales Plan with default input, aggregation, and distribution settings retained](../assets/screenshots/lab02/26-sales-settings.png)

   The created Sales Plan is a copy of FY25 actuals. In the sample data, the All row is **25.87M**, the same as actuals, and differs from Part 1's Target of **30.00M**.

2. Select the **Settings** icon at the far right of the footer and open the **Rows Per Page** dropdown. The initial setting in this example was **Auto**. Select **All** so you can scroll through 85 rows on one page. After setting it, the page indicator was **1 of 1**, and the footer showed **Rows: 85 / Columns: 15**. This does not mean all 85 rows fit on screen simultaneously.

   ![Footer Settings open with Rows Per Page set to Auto](../assets/screenshots/lab02/27-footer-settings.png)

   ![Rows Per Page options All, Auto, 10, 15, 25, 50, and 75](../assets/screenshots/lab02/28-rows-per-page-options.png)

   ![Rows Per Page set to All, showing the Sales Plan columns, All 25.87M, and Target 30.00M](../assets/screenshots/lab02/29-sales-created.png)

3. **Right-click the row label** *Americas* to open the row context menu. Hover over **Collapse**, open the **Specific Level** dropdown in its submenu, and select **Region**. In the screen used here, Region was not an option directly under **Collapse**.

   ![Americas row context menu open](../assets/screenshots/lab02/30-row-menu-inspection.png)

   ![Specific Level displayed in the Collapse submenu](../assets/screenshots/lab02/31-collapse-region-menu.png)

   ![Opening Specific Level and selecting Region from Region, Category, and Sub Category](../assets/screenshots/lab02/32-collapse-specific-level.png)

   ![Collapsed to Region, leaving five rows: All and four regions](../assets/screenshots/lab02/33-region-collapsed.png)

   The resulting five rows are **All, Americas, Asia Pacific, Europe, and Middle East & Africa**. The footer becomes **Rows: 5 / Columns: 15**, while the All-row Sales Plan **25.87M** and Target **30.00M** remain unchanged. The change from 85 to five rows reflects collapsing the displayed hierarchy. It does not delete rows.

lab02-s006.title: Adjust a Subcategory
lab02-s006.markdown:
The Americas sales manager expects growth in Energy & Sports beverages.

4. Select **+** on the *Americas* row, then **+** on the *Beverages* row to display **Energy & Sports**. The column you will change is **Grand Total** for **2026 Sales Plan**. Distinguish it from the adjacent **2026 Target** value.

   ![Americas and Beverages expanded, showing Energy & Sports and three series](../assets/screenshots/lab02/34-americas-beverages-expanded.png)
5. Double-click the **2026 Sales Plan** grand total cell on the **Energy & Sports row**. **Keep the existing text in the formula bar or numeric editor at its existing precision**, append `+8%` to the end, and press Enter. The on-screen `0.49` and expression `0.49+8%` are examples rounded to millions. **Do not replace the actual edit value by retyping 0.49.**

   In the sample data example, the editor shows **`487740.11`**. Press **End** to move to the end and append `+8%` without deleting the value. The expression is **`487740.11+8%`**, and the input preview is **526,759.319**. Check the preview and press **Enter** to confirm.

   ![Opening Energy & Sports annual Sales Plan and checking the original edit value 487740.11](../assets/screenshots/lab02/35-energy-original-precision.png)

   ![Preserving the original value and entering 487740.11+8%, with preview 526,759.319](../assets/screenshots/lab02/36-energy-append-8-percent.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This operation **adds a percentage to the original value**. Typing `+8%` while the existing number is selected replaces the original text. Focus the editor or formula bar, then click again or press **End** to move the cursor to the end before appending. Before confirming, check that **all digits of the original number remain, followed by `+8%`**.
>
> The [official tutorial](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-tutorial/planning/tutorial-1-allocation-collaboration) likewise instructs you to append +8% to the existing value in the formula bar. It does not instruct you to enter a fixed rounded value. If the editor itself shows only a rounded number and you cannot verify the original precision, do not assume precision was preserved based solely on the displayed result. Check the original value or the method for applying a percentage change to the existing value.

**Sample calculation:** 487,740.11 × 1.08 = **526,759.3188**, an increase of 39,019.2088. With display units in millions, Energy & Sports becomes approximately **0.53M**, Beverages **1.53M**, Americas **7.18M**, and All **25.91M**.

![Values saved after the 8% increase, with Sales Plan updated for Energy and its parent levels](../assets/screenshots/lab02/37-energy-increased-result.png)

In this example, the input preview shows three decimal places, while the confirmed edit value shows two. **Do not apply `+8%` again merely to verify the same value.**

| Check | Sample UI display | Calculation example |
|---|---:|---|
| Energy edit value before increase | 487740.11 | Sample data example |
| Preview during input | 526,759.319 | 526759.3188 rounded to three decimal places |
| Energy edit value after confirmation | 526759.32 | The same value rounded to two decimal places |
| All edit value after confirmation | 25905919.61 | Sample calculation |

![Energy edit bar reopened after confirmation, showing 526759.32](../assets/screenshots/lab02/38-energy-increased-editor.png)

![All Sales Plan edit bar showing 25905919.61](../assets/screenshots/lab02/39-all-sales-after-8-percent.png)

These are examples of rounding according to display precision. Target All **30.00M** and FY25 actuals **25.87M** are treated as separate series.

![After saving and restarting the browser, representative values after the 8% increase, series, and expanded rows retained in Reading mode](../assets/screenshots/lab02/40-sales-8-percent-reloaded.png)

> [!NOTE]
> **Retyping a value rounded to 0.49M gives 490,000 × 1.08 = 529,200.** This differs from 526,759.3188 calculated from the original 487,740.11. Both may appear as 0.53 when displayed in millions to two decimal places, so do not replace the original value with a rounded one.

| Row | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Energy & Sports | 0.49 | **0.53** |
| Beverages | 1.49 | **1.53** |
| Americas | 7.14 | **7.18** |
| All | 25.87 | **25.91** |

If you overwrite the original value, for example Energy & Sports becomes 0.00, **use Undo (Ctrl+Z) to reverse the last change and verify at the original precision that it is back to 487,740.11**, then try appending again. Retyping `0.49` as a recovery changes the original value through rounding. If Undo cannot restore it, do not recover from the rounded display; compare with the source actuals and restore the original value.

The increase rolls up automatically to *Beverages* and *Americas*.

lab02-s007.title: Apply a Trend to the Annual Distribution
lab02-s007.markdown:
6. Select the **2026 Sales Plan** annual grand total cell on the **Energy & Sports** row and open the allocation menu. Hover over **Distribute to column with trend**, then select **Input custom value** in the submenu. Enter **4** in **Apply Trend (%)** and select **Apply**. This lets you set the value numerically instead of positioning the slider by eye.

   ![Choosing Distribute to column with trend from the allocation menu for Energy annual Sales Plan](../assets/screenshots/lab02/41-trend-distribution-menu.png)

   ![Trend slider and Input custom value displayed](../assets/screenshots/lab02/42-trend-controls.png)

   ![Entering 4 in Apply Trend (%)](../assets/screenshots/lab02/43-trend-four-percent.png)

After applying, confirm that the annual grand total is unchanged and the period values have changed.

![Saving values displayed immediately after applying, with the distribution across periods changed](../assets/screenshots/lab02/44-trend-applied-result.png)

Scroll horizontally if Q4 is not visible. Trend allocation changes the period values according to the settings.

![Scrolled horizontally to show Q1 through Q4 after trend allocation](../assets/screenshots/lab02/45-trend-q4-visible.png)

| Period | Sample data example |
|---|---:|---|
| Q1 | 109,433.86 |
| Q2 | 123,098.21 |
| Q3 | 138,468.74 |
| Q4 | 155,758.51 |
| Total of four quarters | **526,759.32** |

<details>
<summary>Examples of quarterly values after trend allocation</summary>

![Q1 edit bar after trend allocation: 109433.86012](../assets/screenshots/lab02/46-trend-q1-precision.png)

![Q2 edit bar after trend allocation: 123098.20963](../assets/screenshots/lab02/47-trend-q2-precision.png)

![Q3 edit bar after trend allocation: 138468.74447](../assets/screenshots/lab02/48-trend-q3-precision.png)

![Q4 edit bar after trend allocation: 155758.50578](../assets/screenshots/lab02/49-trend-q4-precision.png)

</details>

In this example, the annual grand totals are approximately **526,759.32** for Energy and **25,905,919.61** for company-wide Sales Plan. You are not adding another 4% to the annual amount; you are changing its distribution across periods while preserving the annual total.

![Energy annual edit value remains 526759.32 after applying the trend](../assets/screenshots/lab02/50-trend-energy-annual.png)

![Company-wide Sales Plan annual edit value also remains 25905919.61](../assets/screenshots/lab02/51-trend-all-annual.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do not interpret 4% as a 4% increase each quarter.** With a column hierarchy of **Year → Quarter → Month Short**, the trend is used to distribute values across periods. Displayed period values vary with settings and data. Confirm that the annual grand total is preserved before and after applying the trend.

Display precision and allocation results depend on the data. When choosing a trend for business use, check the column period hierarchy and the annual grand total after distribution.

lab02-s008.title: Bulk Edit Multiple Regions
lab02-s008.markdown:
APAC and Europe expect Q3 revenue growth in beverages and personal care.

7. On the **Planning** ribbon, select **Bulk Edit**. Initially, Measure and the target levels are unselected, and **Type** is **Set Value**.

   ![Initial Bulk Edit screen with Measure and application levels unselected and Type set to Set Value](../assets/screenshots/lab02/52-bulk-edit-initial.png)

   **Measure:** Select `2026 Sales Plan`.

   **Select Filter:** Use **+ Add Filter** to add the following three dimension filters. Set the operator to **Is**, open the value selector, and select the **checkboxes for the target members**. Do not assume a member is selected simply because you clicked its displayed name; confirm the checkmark. You can select multiple members.

   | Dimension | Operator | Values to select |
   |---|---|---|
   | Region | Is | Asia Pacific, Europe |
   | Category | Is | Beverages, Personal Care |
   | Quarter | Is | Q3 |

   ![Asia Pacific and Europe checked in the Region options](../assets/screenshots/lab02/53-bulk-region-selected.png)

   ![Beverages and Personal Care checked in the Category options](../assets/screenshots/lab02/54-bulk-category-selected.png)

   ![Q3 selected for Quarter](../assets/screenshots/lab02/55-bulk-quarter-selected.png)

   A narrow selector may show only the first member. Reopen each value selector and confirm that both regions and both categories are checked. Scroll within the filter area as needed to verify all three conditions. The trash icon on a filter row deletes that condition.

   **Apply to Row Level:** `Sub Category`. **Apply to Column Level:** `Month Short`. These specify the hierarchy depth at which the edit applies, not the target rows themselves.

   **Type:** Change **Set Value** to **Append By**. **Value:** `8%`.

   ![Changing Type to Append By from the options Set Value, Append By, and Reset Value](../assets/screenshots/lab02/56-bulk-append-by-option.png)

   Move focus out of Value and verify **Append By / 8%** and **Sub Category / Month Short**. In this example, **Apply** became enabled once all settings were complete.

   ![Measure, application levels, Append By, and 8% configured, with Apply enabled](../assets/screenshots/lab02/57-bulk-configured.png)

   ![Region and Category conditions at the top of the filter area, with the Q3 condition below](../assets/screenshots/lab02/58-bulk-filters-top.png)

   Select **Apply** once.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The default Type is Set Value, which replaces existing values.** To increase existing target values by 8%, always select **Append By** before **Apply**. Repeating Apply to verify the result compounds the increase.

This adds 8% to the existing Q3 values for both categories in both regions. The adjustment levels are subcategory and month. In this data, the scope corresponds to 2 regions × 6 subcategories × 3 months, or 36 cells.

**Sample result:** After applying, All becomes approximately **26.10M**, with increases in the targeted Asia Pacific and Europe regions.

![After bulk edit, Sales Plan is All 26.10M, Asia Pacific 9.89M, and Europe 6.22M](../assets/screenshots/lab02/59-bulk-applied-result.png)

| Region | Before (M) | After (M) | Filter scope |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Americas | 7.18 | **7.18** | Excluded |

lab02-s009.markdown:
Numbers without a documented rationale are difficult to explain adequately at a management meeting.

1. Select the **annual grand total cell (Grand Total)** for **2026 Sales Plan** on the **Energy & Sports** row under *Americas* → *Beverages*. A single click is sufficient. Do not open the editor. In this example, it displayed **0.53M**.
2. Open the dropdown to the right of **Comments** at the **top right of the screen**, then select **Add Comment**. Security, Comments, Editing, Save, and other controls appear on the same row as the ribbon tab names. If the UI wording differs from the original source's *Add new comment*, select **Add Comment** as shown on screen.

   ![Energy & Sports Sales Plan annual grand total selected, with Add Comment opened from Comments at the top right](../assets/screenshots/lab02/68-comment-menu.png)

3. Enter the following in the comment editor:

   > Agreed on an 8% revenue increase with the Americas sales manager. Allocated the annual total across quarters using a 4% growth trend.

   Select the **Send** icon once and check the posted text.

> [!NOTE]

>
> **Notes** on the Planning ribbon is a separate feature. It is for fixed annotations rather than threaded discussions.

Comments record the author and timestamp. You can star a comment to mark it as important, or use **Assign to User** to assign someone and turn it into a trackable task. Tasks start as **Open** and can be changed to **Resolved** when addressed.

lab02-s012.title: Part 4: Request Approval
lab02-s012.markdown:
This part separates **the overall submission status updated by the submitter** from **two approval stages handled by the regional manager and headquarters manager**. The instructions below are based on [configuring approval workflows](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-how-to-configure-approval-workflows). Verify the configuration field names, stages you can add, and status options in your workshop environment.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The first level manages the overall submission status.** The official detailed configuration article places submission statuses such as In Progress, Submitted, and Reopened in the first level, and assigns approvers to subsequent levels. To request approval from both a regional manager and a headquarters manager, configure separate approval levels.

The intended columns and owners for this exercise are listed below. Create them separately from Part 3's progress-tracking `Status` column.

| Column name | Owner | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Task Status` | Submitter | Manage submission and resubmission status |
| `Regional Manager` | Regional approver | Approve or reject at the first approval stage |
| `Finance Director` | Headquarters approver | Approve or reject at the second approval stage |

1. Open `Plan Intro` and select **Approval** on the **Model** ribbon. If a configuration already exists, check its column names, owners, stages, and notification settings.
2. Check the status options in the first level and name the overall submission-status column `Task Status`. Select the submitter who will update this column. Name the next approval level `Regional Manager` and select the regional approver. Do not count the submission-status column as an approval stage simply from the numbers shown on screen.
3. Set up a `Finance Director` approval level and select the headquarters approver. If there are insufficient stages, use **Add** as described in the official instructions to add an approval level. Verify **three columns in total: one submission-status column and two approval columns**, their owners, and approval order, then select **Next**. Verify Add and the level names in the actual screen.
4. Turn on **Reset on Rejection**. Official documentation says it is off by default and, when the final approver rejects, returns the preceding submission and approval statuses to In Progress or Reopened. Verify the status names and affected stages in the workshop environment.
5. Check **Teams Notifications**. Official documentation says notifications to approvers on approval requests and to submitters on approval or rejection are on by default. **Submitting, approving, or rejecting with these enabled may send actual Teams notifications to the configured people.** Notify recipients beforehand if you will send notifications. To test status transitions without sending notifications, turn both off and also check whether any existing On Change Formula sends notifications.
6. Select **Submit** to create the configuration. Check the three columns, `Task Status`, `Regional Manager`, and `Finance Director`, their status options and owners, then verify retention after saving and reloading. Submit here creates the workflow configuration; submitting individual plan values for approval is step 8.

> [!NOTE]
> **A submitter and one approver** can perform a single-stage handoff. **A two-stage flow with different people handling regional and headquarters approval** requires a submitter and two approvers. If the same person is assigned to both approval stages, assess whether this is appropriate for separation-of-duties requirements.
>
> Select real users who will handle approval from the approver candidates. If they do not appear, check that the users exist, their access to the Plan and model, and the workshop environment's configuration. Do not assume Microsoft Entra B2B guests are universally unsupported; verify them in advance following the [Module 00 prerequisites](00-prerequisites.md). Sessions and billing roles when participants actually perform operations are verification items in [Module 08](08-sizing-and-governance.md).

lab02-s013.title: Test the Workflow
lab02-s013.markdown:
7. Using the submitter's account, expand *Asia Pacific → Beverages* to **Sub Category** and the target year's columns to **Month**. For every leaf cell in the **2026 Sales Plan** scope you will change, record the year, month, region, Category, Sub Category, scenario, and pre-change value. Also record regional and All totals for the same scope. Rounded aggregate values alone cannot restore the detail. If you cannot record all leaf values, use an exact per-user backup / export prepared by the instructor beforehand. If no restoration source is available, do not change values or practice resubmission after rejection; limit the exercise to explaining status transitions. Once a restoration source is secured, return to the same *Asia Pacific → Beverages* grand total cell, append `+10%` to the existing number once only, and press Enter. Do not infer the current cell value or date keys from 2026 in the column name.
8. In the **Task Status** column on the same *Asia Pacific → Beverages* row, select **Submitted**. Check the statuses and owners of Task Status, Regional Manager, and Finance Director. According to the official detailed instructions, submitting sets the first approval stage to Pending; after approval, it passes to the next stage. Submitted does not mean final approval is complete.

lab02-s014.title: Handoff After Submission
lab02-s014.markdown:
- Have the regional approver open the same target row under their own identity and approve it. Verify the handoff to the headquarters approver by checking the owner, target values, and each column's status.
- Have the headquarters approver reject it under their own identity, and check how Task Status and the preceding approval statuses reset. **Do not resubmit immediately after rejection.** Explicitly restore the target monthly / Sub Category values from the pre-change record or pre-exercise backup. Dividing the annual total by 1.10 alone does not establish that the original detail distribution has been restored.
- Save the plan and, after a normal reload, confirm that the target leaf values, regional totals, and All total match the pre-change records. Then resubmit the restored plan and complete regional approval followed by headquarters approval. If restoration itself becomes a new approval target, check that status too.
- Verify Teams notification settings separately from actual receipt in the recipient's own Teams. A sent indicator alone does not establish receipt.
- **Reset on rejection does not guarantee automatic restoration of input values.** Do not replace original values with rounded displays; compare target cells and aggregate values after saving.

lab02-s015.title: What You Have Accomplished
lab02-s015.markdown:
This module covers top-down allocation using the previous year's mix, bottom-up planning with regional adjustments, sharing the assumptions behind numbers, and a regional / headquarters approval flow with a separate submission status. The sample scenario places an 11-day consolidation process in a single sheet.

In the next module, you will work through concrete numbers for a $30 million revenue target and a $12.5 million gross profit target.

lab02-s016.title: Knowledge Check
lab02-s016.markdown:
1. Why copy a measure instead of entering values directly into *2025 Gross Revenue*?
2. After locking Q1 and Q2 and increasing the annual total, what happens on the next revision if you forget to unlock them?
3. How does **Distribute to column with trend** differ from ordinary allocation?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Native columns and semantic model measures are read-only. Copying creates an editable series while retaining actuals as a baseline.
2. Q1 and Q2 remain excluded from the next allocation, so the entire change is allocated to unlocked quarters. This may go unnoticed until someone spots an odd period mix.
3. It distributes the annual total across periods along a growth curve rather than proportionally or equally.

</details>
